about: Measured human skin colour data the skin-tone model is built from. Run `python3 -m tools.build_skin_model` after editing.

populations.source: Lu et al. (2026), 'Skin Colour Does Not Define Ethnicity: Quantifying Variation and Overlap Across Diverse Populations', Skin Research and Technology, Table 2. https://doi.org/10.1111/srt.70343 (open access, CC BY 4.0). Values are mean (SD) of in-vivo CIELAB measurements.

facial_hue.source: Wang, Xiao, Wuerger, Cheung & Luo (2015), 'Measuring Human Skin Colour', 23rd Color and Imaging Conference, pp. 230-234. 188 subjects, 10 body locations incl. forehead, cheek, cheekbone, chin, nose tip; CM700d spectrophotometer and PR650 tele-spectroradiometer, D65 / CIE 1931.
notes: Hue agrees within 2 degrees between contact and non-contact instruments.
Caucasian and Oriental: lighter skin is less chromatic. African: darker skin is less chromatic. South Asian: varies mainly in lightness.

monk.source: Monk Skin Tone Scale (Ellis Monk, Google, 2022), released under CC BY 4.0. https://skintone.google/ ; hex values as listed at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monk_Skin_Tone_Scale

ita.source: Chardon, Cretois & Hourseau (1991), 'Skin colour typology and suntanning pathways', Int J Cosmet Sci 13:191-208. ITA = atan((L* - 50) / b*) in degrees.
